pattern_explanation: Both languages inherited this family word from the same Latin source, parentem, so the forms stayed close. Over time, however, the Portuguese form narrowed toward the general idea of a relative, while the English form kept the meaning of parent, so the spelling looks familiar but the meaning differs.
false_friend_warning: The Portuguese word that means relative looks almost identical to the English word parent, so learners may assume it means parent; it does not. Be careful with the Portuguese word for cousin as well, because it resembles the English word prime but has an unrelated meaning.
